nos.title: Manually remove, change and install low voltage, single and three phase energy meters

performance_criteria.text: obtain job specification or work order from responsible authority

select and use appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) as per occupational health and safety guidelines Personal protective equipment: hard working caps, protective glasses, rubber gloves, fall arrest and restraint, safety footwear, fire-resistant clothing, etc.

use and maintain appropriate tools and equipment in accordance with the tasks \Tools and equipment: e.g. insulated hand tools; drills; hacksaw; hand tools; testing equipment; insulation testers; crimping tools; wires and cables of various colours and sizes; heat shrink sleeving and flexible conduit; terminals and connectors; electrical tape; etc. To be competent, the user/ individual on the job must be able to:
verify the distance between the poles or cables is as per standards
check the underground and/or overhead cables are laid correctly as per work order
plan and locate the area inside or outside the customer’s premise after assessing possible risks
check that the identified area is accessible to carry out installation, meter testing, commissioning, reading, recording and maintenance

ensure the energy meter has passed quality assessments set by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and is ready for installation Consumer meters: Low Voltage(LV) meters; single phase meter (two wires system) and three phase meters (four wires system)
inspect the facility’s wiring system and recognize any possible risks to be isolated or common phase or looping of phase of two or more consumers
inform all affected parties of the intended work plan in advance prior to disconnecting power supply line To be competent, the user/individual on the job must be able to:
install the energy meter and supportive equipment using insulated tools and devices as per organizational procedures Supportive equipment: e.g. meter box, junction box, distribution bus bar, etc.
equip the energy meter with various anti- tampering features as per regulations and organizational procedures

establish immunity against various types of external factors in accordance with relevant regulations External factors: magnetic induction, vibration, electrostatic discharge, switching transients, surge voltages, oblique suspension and harmonics

ensure the energy meter displays one or more of the following parameters depending upon the tariff requirement for different categories of consumers Measuring parameters: cumulative reactive energy, average power factor, time of energy use, apparent power, maximum demand, phase voltage and line currents
check the energy meter for earth leakage indication as per relevant regulations Regulations: Central Electricity Authority (installation and operation of meters) Regulations, 2006
test and calibrate the energy meter using appropriate testing devices in line with organizational quality standards and regulations
identify and escalate unresolved problems to appropriate authority for rectifications To be competent, the user/individual on the job must be able to:

establish the reason for changing the energy meter from responsible source in order to plan out the work Reasons: discrepancies (stoppage of meter, erratic consumption output, broken seal, burning or damage of meter), service disconnection
replace the same with a duly tested energy meter as per instructions given in organizational guidelines and regulations
test to confirm that the replaced energy meter conforms to required work specifications
check that any replaced or repaired equipment is working properly, and customer’s problems are resolved efficiently To be competent, the user/ individual on the job must be able to:

identify the Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) to be installed; such as smart meters (single-phase and 3-phase), communication infrastructure, Head-End System (HES), Meter Data Management System (MDMS)

determine the communication network/technology to be used; such as Broadband over PowerLine (BPL), Power Line Communications (PLCs), Fiber Optic Communication, Zigbee, 6LoWPAN, Bluetooth, Fixed Radio Frequency or public networks (e.g., landline, cellular, paging)

evaluate key factors for selecting an appropriate installation site such as network reliability, availability of existing network; convenient location for the user/customer; required signal strength etc.
confirm the availability of required tools, equipment, materials, hardware and software for installing smart meter To be competent, the user/ individual on the job must be able to:
install smart meter box and smart metering hardware
perform wiring and cable connections
install the In-Home Display (IHD)
configure smart meter to establish required connectivity with the Head-End System (HES)
enter the IP address as provided through the HES for enabling networking capabilities of the smart meter To be competent, the user/individual on the job must be able to:
test the smart meter for potential hardware issues; such as orientation of meter; improper connections; using a different port instead of recommended etc.
check the connections, features, switches within the smart metering network for required functioning
test the In-Home Display (IHD) for required connectivity and functioning
check the communication network (Wireless Area Network (WAN), Home Area Network (HAN) etc.) to evaluate two-way communication capability between smart meter and HES
verify that the smart meter cover is securely fitted to ensure adequate protection against extreme environmental conditions
record data such as customer identification number, meter ID, its hardware and software configuration, name plate details, make, type i.e. 1 Phase or 3 Phase, etc. (as per requirement of utility)
prepare work reports for the tasks performed

instruct the user/customer the various procedures through which they can avail of customer services offered Customer services: viewing meter readings and reports; updating personal information such as mobile number, email; generating service requests; viewing recharge history, present balance etc.
clear the worksite to ensure no hazardous and waste materials are present To be competent, the user/individual on the job must be able to:

nos.title: Apply basic health and safety practices for power related work

performance_criteria.text: use protective clothing/equipment for specific tasks and work conditions Protective clothing: leather or asbestos gloves, flame proof aprons, flame proof overalls buttoned to neck, cuff less (without folds) trousers, reinforced footwear, helmets/hard hats, cap and shoulder covers, ear defenders/plugs, safety boots, knee pads, particle masks, glasses/goggles/visors Equipment: hand and face shields, machine guards, residual current devices, shields, dust sheets, respirator

identify job-site hazards and possible causes of risks/accident at the workplace Hazards: electrical hazards; sharp edged and heavy tools; heated metals; oxyfuel and gas cylinders; welding radiation; hazardous surfaces; hazardous substances; physical hazards possible causes of risk and accident: physical actions; not following instructions; inattention; sickness and incapacity; health; not taking safety precautions
use standard safe working practices when working at heights, confined areas, trenches and with electrical equipment
follow warning signs and symbols while working with electrical systems Warning signs: Danger plate, high voltage area, out of service, etc.
ensure positive isolation of electrical equipment and system as per the given standards
identify any abnormalities in electrical equipment or system viz temperature, pressure, flow of current etc.
use various methods of accident prevention in the work environment
use proper scaffolds, elevated platforms and ladders for working at height
inspect various tools and plants (T & P) routinely for any signs of oil, water leakages
store flammable materials and machine lubricating oil safely and correctly
check that the emission and pollution control devices are working properly in line with environmental policy standards
inform the relevant authorities about any abnormal situation/behavior of any equipment/system without delay To be competent, the user/ individual on the job must be able to:
use various appropriate fire extinguishers for different types of fires correctly Types of fires: Class A, B, C, D and E
use appropriate rescue techniques during fire hazard
use good housekeeping practices at all times to avoid accidental fire To be competent, the user/ individual on the job must be able to:
administer appropriate first aid to the victims for the relevant injuries Injuries: Bleeding, burns, choking, electric shock, poisoning etc.
